overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on any allegation. Declined to review the handwritten-notes claim and referred it to the Supervisor of Records.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair limited his December 19, 2012 comments to existing draft order conditions and barred him from proposing new conditions.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission Chair therefore had discretion to decide who could speak at the meeting and for how long.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to discuss a November 29, 2012 letter from an engineering firm submitted regarding the project.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to discuss any topic.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to provide handwritten notes drafted by a member, which he said were used at a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to review this allegation, and refer the complainant to the Supervisor of Records with any questions about filing an appeal with his office.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged an applicant met or communicated with Commission staff before a ZBA meeting without public notice or public access.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission is not required to post notice or open to the public a meeting involving only its staff, since it does not involve communication between or among a quorum of a public body's members.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the December 19, 2012 minutes omitted critical discussion of his request to add new conditions to the project order.
allegations.key_passage: While the minutes may not reflect every detail regarding this discussion, we find the minutes were sufficiently accurate to be in substantial compliance with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.
